newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - July 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - July 9.

text.p: This daily press summary is produced for Reuters by the Broadcast Monitoring Company, which is responsible for its contents. PENSIONS MIS-SALES MAY COST 4BN POUNDS STG, SAY INSURERS

The Association of British Insurers warned yesterday that the cost of clearing up the pensions mis-selling scandal may rise as high as 4bn pounds stg after an additional 500m pounds hit caused by the abolition of tax credits for pension schemes. In a continuance of their "naming and shaming" policy the government will publicly castigate two more companies on Wednesday. Up to now only two companies of the worst 24 have resolved more than 10 per cent of their cases, despite strict deadlines to complete 90 per cent by the end of the year.
-- GERMANY SET TO GIVE EUROFIGHTER GO-AHEAD

The German cabinet is expected to give its formal backing to the Eurofighter project on Friday, ending months of uncertainty for its partners. The decision to go-ahead follows a deal between finance minister Theo Waigel and defence minister Volker Ruhe over financing the project until 2001.
-- CBI CALLS FOR MORE TRANSPORT SPENDING

The Confederation of British Industries has told the Government that it must switch its spending priorities to provide more funds for transport. They called for an additional public spending of 2bn pounds a year and the creation of a "problem busting group"" reporting directly to the minister of transport. The crisis is so bad "that action cannot wait for longer term strategies", said CBI deputy director-general, Peter Agar.
-- EU RIGHT TO INTEREST ON LATE PAYMENT LIKELY

The European Commission is expected to accept a report that recommends a statutory right to interest on commercial debts and a requirement for public bodies to pay interest if they fail to settle bills within 60 days. Should they do so this would be the first step towards an EU directive putting the force of law behind efforts to reduce the incidence of late payment of commercial debt, a phenomenon that has worsened since Brussels initialled recommendations two years ago.
-- TECS ASSURED OF WELFARE-TO-WORK ROLE

Training and Enterprise Councils, the public bodies designed to improve employment skills, have been assured by the education and employment secretary, David Blunkett that they will play a "critical role" in the work-to-welfare scheme. Chris Humphries, chief executive of the TEC national council said he was "very encouraged" by Mr Blunkett's words. Up to now the TECS had been worried that they would only be offered a limited role in the scheme.
-- ENGINEERING SEES FALLING EXPORT LEVELS

Export levels in the engineering sector are at their lowest since the early 1990s, the Engineering Employers Federation said on Tuesday. In its latest quarterly report on the industry, the EEF said that confidence in engineering companies was suffering because of the increasingly strong pound, leaving many unable to compete in the export market.
-- ING BUYS US LIFE INSURER FOR $2.2BN

ING, the Dutch banking and insurance group, agreed yesterday to pay $2.2bn (1.3bn pounds stg) for US insurer Equitable of Iowa. ING chairman, Aad Jacobs, said that the US insurance market was the largest and "most innovative" in the world; "ING could not ignore it." The deal will roughly double the size of ING's life insurance in the US.
-- EMU HOPES LEAD TO SURGE IN ITALIAN BONDS

Italian bond prices surged on Tuesday after renewed confidence that Italy will be part of the first wave to join the Emu in 1999. Yields on 10-year Italian bonds fell to 6.52 per cent from 6.6 per cent on Monday, less than a percentage higher than German paper. David Brown, chief European economist at Bear Stearns in London described the rally as having the momentum of "an express train".
-- BESPAK POISED TO DOUBLE ASTHMA INHALER INVESTMENT

Healthcare group Bespak is planning to double its investment in asthma inhaler products to meet new environmental regulations which ban the use of CFCs in aerosols. Investment will rise from 6.8m pounds last year to 13m this and will be kept at a similarly high level for the following two years. The extra spending will be funded from the company's own cash flow.
-- BT/MCI MERGER SET FOR FINAL HURDLE

British Telecom and MCI are increasingly confident that their proposed $20bn (11.8bn pounds stg) merger will go ahead in the autumn following approval this week from the US Department of Justice. The merger, the largest transatlantic deal to date, involves BT's acquisition of the 80 per cent of MCI that it does not already own.
